back: Encoder RNN reads the source; its last state initialises the decoder RNN, which emits a softmax over the target vocabulary at each step and feeds back the previous word.
Feed the gold previous token as decoder input during training. Stabilises learning; causes exposure bias at inference.
Train/inference mismatch (gold vs own inputs). Scheduled sampling: anneal the probability of using the model's own predictions.
Greedy takes the arg-max each step. Beam search keeps the $b$ best prefixes by summed log-probability; $b=1$ is greedy; a heuristic without guarantee.
Products of probabilities underflow; $\log$ turns them into sums. Sum log-softmax, not logits.
All information about the source must fit in one fixed-size vector (and gradients must travel the whole recurrent chain), so long inputs degrade.
$\alpha_t=\operatorname{softmax}(e_t)$ over source positions; $c_t=\sum_i\alpha_{t,i}h_i\in\mathbb{R}^H$; alignment matrix $(T_t,T_s)$ with unit row sums.
Bahdanau queries with the previous decoder state $s_{t-1}$ (additive score); Luong with the current $s_t$ (dot, general or concat scores).
$\bar\alpha_i=\bar c^\top h_i$; $\bar e=\alpha\odot(\bar\alpha-\alpha^\top\bar\alpha)$; $\bar h_i$ gets $\alpha_i\bar c$ (value path) plus $U_a^\top\bar z_i$ (key path).

front: How to mask padding in attention
back: Set padded scores to a very negative value before the softmax so their weight is 0 and others still sum to 1.
$\operatorname{Var}(q\cdot k)=d$ for unit-variance entries; scaling keeps scores in a range where the softmax is not saturated.

front: Query, key, value reading of attention
back: Query = decoder state; keys = what we match against; values = what we average (here the encoder states). Self-attention takes all three from the same sequence.
Not reliably: they look interpretable, but can be changed without altering predictions on some tasks. Validate with ablations.
